stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group on the waiting list

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They hypothesized that the color of the drinks would affect flavor identification.

**Participants.** The sample was 70 adult volunteers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

**Results.** The group whose drinks had mismatched colors: mean flavors named correctly (out of 10) = 4.1. The group whose drinks had matching colors: mean flavors named correctly (out of 10) = 7.8. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Do rewards increase motivation?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 60 preschool children who liked drawing were randomly assigned to draw for a promised certificate or to draw with no reward. A week later, during free play, the rewarded children chose to draw for a mean of 6.5 minutes and the unrewarded children for 13.8 minutes (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** In a study of 200 call-center workers, half were randomly assigned to receive a bonus for each sale. Over a month, the bonus group made a mean of 41 sales and the comparison group a mean of 33 (p = 0.02). When the bonus ended, the bonus group's sales fell to a mean of 30.

**Source C.** A survey of 500 university students found that students who said they studied mainly because they found their subject interesting had higher grades and reported less burnout than students who said they studied mainly for grades or money (r = +0.40 between interest and grades).

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion?

options.why: Correct. An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.
Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.
The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.
Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.

questions.explanation: An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.

questions.stem: After the tone is sounded many times with no food, a dog stops salivating to the tone. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Acquisition is in classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned.
Correct. Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.
Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.
Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.

questions.explanation: Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 12, 6, 23, 10, 9, 9, 8. What is the mean of the scores?

options.why: That is the median.
Correct. Add the scores (77) and divide by 7.
That is the range.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 6, 8, 9, 9, 10, 12, 23. Add the scores (77) and divide by 7. The one very high score pulls the mean (11) above the median (9), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes implicit memory?

options.text: The shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance
options.why: That describes structural encoding.

options.text: The deep encoding of a word based on its meaning
options.why: That describes semantic encoding.

options.text: The encoding that requires attention and conscious effort
options.why: That describes effortful processing.

options.text: The memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall
options.why: Correct. This is what implicit memory means.

questions.explanation: Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.

questions.stem: Eight people with social anxiety meet weekly with one therapist, share their experiences and practice skills together. Which kind of therapy is this?

options.why: Correct. Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.
Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.
Hypnosis is a state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories.
Active listening is the technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says.

questions.explanation: Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.

questions.stem: A therapist keeps every appointment, honors his commitments and protects the trust his clients place in him. Which ethical principle is he following?

options.why: Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.
Correct. Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.
Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.

questions.explanation: Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.

questions.stem: Hearing a song from her school days brings back a flood of memories for Tina. The song is acting as which of the following?

options.why: Recall is the retrieval of information without any cues, as in an essay question.
Recognition is the identification of previously learned information when it is presented, as in a multiple-choice question.
State-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same physical state as when the information was learned.
Correct. A retrieval cue is a stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind.

questions.explanation: A retrieval cue is a stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: A case study examines one individual in depth.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: A mother's employer changes her to night shifts, so she sees her son less. In ecological systems theory, her workplace is part of which system?

options.why: The microsystem is in ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school.
The macrosystem is in ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child.
Correct. The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.
The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.explanation: The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: To study, Omar arranges his notes into main topics, then subtopics, then details. Which encoding strategy is he using?

options.why: Correct. A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.
Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.
Chunking is the organizing of items into familiar, manageable units.
Distributed practice is study that is spread out over several sessions.

questions.explanation: A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.

questions.stem: A study tested only male university students, so critics doubt that its findings apply to older adults or to women. Which quality of the study are they questioning?

options.why: Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.
Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.
A convenience sample is a sample made up of whoever is easiest for the researcher to reach.
Correct. Generalizability is the extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample.

questions.explanation: Generalizability is the extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample.

questions.stem: An eight-month-old learns about a rattle by shaking it, looking at it and putting it in her mouth. Which of Piaget's stages is she in?

options.why: The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.
Correct. The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.

questions.explanation: The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.

questions.stem: Leah is sure a fact is true but cannot remember whether she read it in a textbook or saw it in a film. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.
The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.
Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.
Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.

questions.explanation: Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.

questions.stem: Selye found that animals under prolonged stress passed through alarm, then resistance, then exhaustion. What is this three-phase pattern called?

options.why: Correct. The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.
The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.
The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.
The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.

questions.explanation: The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values?

options.why: Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.
Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.
The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.
Correct. Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.

questions.explanation: Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.

questions.stem: A charity first asks people to sign a petition and a week later asks the same people for a donation. Which technique is this?

options.why: A social norm is a rule for accepted and expected behavior in a group.
Correct. The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.
The peripheral route to persuasion is persuasion that works through surface cues, such as an attractive or famous speaker.
The central route to persuasion is persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully.

questions.explanation: The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.stem: A hearing test finds the quietest tone that Aiko can detect on 50 percent of trials. What does this test measure?

options.why: Weber's law is the principle that two stimuli must differ by a constant proportion, not a constant amount, to be noticed.
Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.
Correct. The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.
Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.

questions.explanation: The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice?

options.why: Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.
Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.
Correct. Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.

questions.explanation: Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.

questions.stem: Two hostile groups of campers became friendly after they had to work together to repair the camp's water supply. The repair was an example of which of the following?

options.why: The false consensus effect is the tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors.
Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.
Correct. A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.
Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.

questions.explanation: A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.

questions.stem: Ed feels strong resentment toward his sister but treats her with exaggerated kindness and praise. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Correct. Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.
Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.explanation: Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.

questions.stem: Wearing masks in a large, excited crowd, normally law-abiding fans begin smashing windows. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.
Correct. Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.
Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.
Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.

questions.explanation: Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.

questions.stem: At seventy, Mr. Park is slower than he used to be at solving unfamiliar logic puzzles. Which kind of intelligence has declined?

options.why: The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.
Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.
Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.
Correct. Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.

questions.explanation: Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.

questions.stem: During deep sleep, the body releases growth hormone and repairs muscle tissue. This best supports which function of sleep?

options.why: The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.
Correct. Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.
Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.

questions.explanation: Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.stem: A researcher reports that two variables are related, with r = +0.62. What is this number called?

options.why: A positive correlation is a relationship in which two variables rise and fall together.
Correct. The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.
The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.
A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.

questions.explanation: The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.

questions.stem: In a noisy cafeteria, Carla follows only her friend's voice and ignores the conversations around her. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.
Correct. Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.
Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.
A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.

questions.explanation: Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the cognitive perspective?

options.text: The view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood
options.why: That describes the psychodynamic perspective.

options.text: The view that disorders involve behaviors that once helped survival but are now harmful
options.why: That describes the evolutionary perspective.

options.text: The view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking
options.why: Correct. This is what the cognitive perspective means.

options.text: The view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination
options.why: That describes the sociocultural perspective.

questions.explanation: The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.

questions.stem: Lin gives up her seat on the bus to an elderly stranger who can never repay her. Which norm is guiding her?

options.why: The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.
The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.
Correct. The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.
Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

questions.explanation: The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.

questions.stem: A questionnaire tells Ravi that his top character traits are curiosity, fairness and humor, and encourages him to use them daily. These traits are called which of the following?

options.why: Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.
Correct. Signature strengths is the positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person.
Positive psychology is the scientific study of the strengths and conditions that help people and communities thrive.
Resilience is the ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship.

questions.explanation: Signature strengths is the positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped?

options.why: Correct. Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.
A fixed mindset is the belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed.
An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.
An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.

questions.explanation: Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes nurture?

options.text: The influence of inherited genetic factors on behavior and mental processes
options.why: That describes nature.

options.text: The influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes
options.why: Correct. This is what nurture means.

options.text: Research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity
options.why: That describes a twin study.

options.text: Research that compares adopted children with their biological and adoptive relatives
options.why: That describes an adoption study.

questions.explanation: Nurture is the influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input?

options.why: An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.
A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.
Correct. A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.
A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.

questions.explanation: A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.

questions.stem: After an argument with his roommate, Luis talks to him directly to settle the disagreement. Which kind of coping is this?

options.why: Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.
Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.
Correct. Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.

questions.explanation: Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes extraversion?

options.text: The Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic
options.why: Correct. This is what extraversion means.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody
options.why: That describes emotional stability.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative
options.why: That describes agreeableness.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things
options.why: That describes openness to experience.

questions.explanation: Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.55. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: A theory says that neurons alternate firing, like soldiers taking turns shooting, to keep up with sounds faster than one neuron can fire. Which theory is this?

options.why: Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.
Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.
Frequency theory is the theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound.
Correct. Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.

questions.explanation: Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: When a crisis hits, Maria phones her friends, checks on her children and organizes the neighbors to help one another. Which response to stress is this?

options.why: Health psychology is the field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness.
Distress is the negative stress that harms well-being and performance.
Correct. The tend-and-befriend response is the response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support.
Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.

questions.explanation: The tend-and-befriend response is the response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also test hypotheses.
Experiments also use numerical data.
Sample size does not determine the research method.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes applied behavior analysis?

options.text: The use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones
options.why: Correct. This is what applied behavior analysis means.

options.text: The technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them
options.why: That describes biofeedback.

options.text: The behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus
options.why: That describes aversion therapy.

options.text: The behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards
options.why: That describes a token economy.

questions.explanation: Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.

questions.stem: A four-year-old uses a banana as a telephone and 'calls' her grandmother. Which kind of play is this?

options.why: Correct. Pretend play is the play in which children act out imaginary roles and situations.
Emerging adulthood is the period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence.
The social clock is a culture's preferred timing for life events such as marriage, parenthood and retirement.
The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.

questions.explanation: Pretend play is the play in which children act out imaginary roles and situations.

questions.stem: 'Because I said so' is the only explanation that Tara's parents ever give for their many strict rules. Which parenting style is this?

options.why: Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.
Correct. Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.

questions.explanation: Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.

questions.stem: A researcher destroys a tiny part of a rat's hypothalamus and observes how its eating changes. Which research technique is this?

options.why: An EEG is a recording of the electrical waves that sweep across the brain's surface.
An fMRI is a scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow.
A case study is an in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage.
Correct. Lesioning is the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function.

questions.explanation: Lesioning is the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the DSM?

options.text: The criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships
options.why: That describes dysfunction.

options.text: The criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects
options.why: That describes deviation from the social norm.

options.text: The criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person
options.why: That describes distress.

options.text: The American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders
options.why: Correct. This is what the DSM means.

questions.explanation: The DSM is the American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders.

questions.stem: At a normal weight, Tara secretly eats huge amounts of food and then makes herself vomit. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.
Correct. Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.
Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight.
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.

questions.explanation: Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A case study examines one individual in depth.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.
This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: With her eyes closed, Uma can still touch her nose with her fingertip. Which sense makes this possible?

options.why: The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
Correct. Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

questions.explanation: Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 80 university students. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.
Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: A therapist helps a client replace the thought 'I failed one test, so I am stupid' with 'One test does not define me.' Which technique is this?

options.why: The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.
Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.
Correct. Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.
Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.

questions.explanation: Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.
Debriefing happens after the study.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The average number of hours slept per night
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

options.text: The level of stress at home
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: A dentist's drill causes pain, and soon the sound of the drill alone makes Ben tense. Becoming tense at the sound is which of the following?

options.why: The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.
Correct. The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.
The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.explanation: The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.

questions.stem: A nine-year-old takes pride in finishing his school projects well and compares his work with classmates' work. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.
Correct. Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.

questions.explanation: Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the unconscious?

options.text: In psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior
options.why: Correct. This is what the unconscious means.

options.text: A personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings
options.why: That describes a projective test.

options.text: In psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality
options.why: That describes a defense mechanism.

options.text: In humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential
options.why: That describes the self-actualizing tendency.

questions.explanation: The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.

questions.stem: To teach a dolphin to jump through a hoop, a trainer first rewards swimming near the hoop, then touching it, then passing through it. Which technique is this?

options.why: The law of effect is Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by good outcomes become more likely and those followed by bad outcomes become less likely.
Learned helplessness is the passive giving up that follows repeated experiences of being unable to avoid bad events.
A primary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as food or water, that satisfies a biological need and is rewarding without learning.
Correct. Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.

questions.explanation: Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The rats given the nausea-causing injection were several months older
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: The two groups differed in preference for sweetened water at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the type of injection given after drinking
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Hallucinations and delusions are experiences that are present in schizophrenia but absent in healthy functioning. Which kind of symptom are they?

options.why: Correct. A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.
The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.
A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.

questions.explanation: A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.

questions.stem: Ines cannot stand doing the same task twice and becomes restless whenever life is predictable. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Correct. Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.

questions.explanation: Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.text: Whether a small request came first
options.why: This is the independent variable.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.

options.text: The percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates?

options.why: The availability heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind.
The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.
Correct. The representativeness heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates.
The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.

questions.explanation: The representativeness heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates.

questions.stem: A sleeper's EEG shows large, slow delta waves, and she is very difficult to wake. Which stage of sleep is she in?

options.why: Correct. NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.
NREM stage 1 is the brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling.
REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.
The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.

questions.explanation: NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.

questions.stem: After a long race, a runner feels little pain and a sense of well-being. Which neurotransmitters are most likely responsible?

options.why: Correct. Endorphins is the neurotransmitters that reduce pain and increase pleasure.
Substance P is the neurotransmitter that carries pain messages to the brain.
GABA is the brain's main inhibitory neurotransmitter.
Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.

questions.explanation: Endorphins is the neurotransmitters that reduce pain and increase pleasure.

questions.stem: When Ana becomes too hot, she sweats, and when she is cold, she shivers, keeping her body temperature near 37 degrees Celsius. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.
Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.
Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.
The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.

questions.stem: A harder pinch does not make an individual neuron fire a stronger impulse; each impulse has the same strength. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The all-or-nothing principle is the rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all.
Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.
Depolarization is the change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative.
The threshold is the level of stimulation that must be reached for a neuron to fire.

questions.explanation: The all-or-nothing principle is the rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: A case study examines one individual in depth.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: Karl, who dislikes his colleague, is convinced that the colleague hates him. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.
Correct. Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.
Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.
Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.explanation: Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.

questions.stem: After getting food poisoning from fish, Carl feels sick at the smell of fish for years. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.
Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.
Correct. A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.
Biological preparedness is the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others.

questions.explanation: A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon?

options.text: Forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory
options.why: That describes encoding failure.

options.text: In psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness
options.why: That describes repression.

options.text: The temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows
options.why: Correct. This is what the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon means.

options.text: The disruption of older memories by new learning
options.why: That describes retroactive interference.

questions.explanation: The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.

questions.stem: A coach performs a correct free throw slowly so that her players can watch and copy it. The coach is doing which of the following?

options.why: Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.
Insight learning is the sudden realization of the solution to a problem.
Correct. Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.
A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.

questions.explanation: Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing?

options.why: Protection from harm is the requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible.
An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.
Correct. Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.
Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.

questions.explanation: Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.

questions.stem: Zoe is taking classes in art, biology and law to work out what she wants, and she has not decided yet. Which identity status is this?

options.why: Correct. Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.
Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.explanation: Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.

questions.stem: Damage to a network running through the brainstem leaves a patient in a coma, unable to be woken. Which structure is damaged?

options.why: The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex.
The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.
Correct. The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.
The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.

questions.explanation: The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of flavor identification

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of flavor identification.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Flavor identification was defined as the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group with mismatched colors named fewer flavors correctly. On average, the value was 4.1 for the group whose drinks had mismatched colors and 7.8 for the group whose drinks had matching colors, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 70 adult volunteers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group with mismatched colors named fewer flavors correctly. (4.1 compared with 7.8).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the color of the drinks affects flavor identification. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the color of the drinks. The finding illustrates sensory interaction: one sense, here vision, influences another, here taste.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Do rewards increase motivation?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Rewards increase a behavior while they last, but they can reduce intrinsic motivation, so the behavior falls when the rewards stop.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, children promised a certificate later chose to draw for 6.5 minutes, compared with 13.8 minutes for children who were not rewarded.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through intrinsic and extrinsic motivation: the reward gave the children an external reason for drawing, which weakened their desire to draw for its own sake.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, workers paid a bonus made more sales (41 compared with 33), but their sales fell to 30 when the bonus ended.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through operant conditioning: the bonus acted as positive reinforcement, which increased the behavior, and when reinforcement stopped the behavior declined (extinction).

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
